body.p: Applicant would like to thank Patent Examiner Kyle A. Cook for the courtesies extended to Applicant's representative Karin Loyola, during the telephone interview between the Examiner and Applicant's representative, conducted on January 3, 2025. Prior to the January 3, 2025 telephone interview, Applicant's representative sent to Examiner Cook for review proposed amended claims and remarks with respect to the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejections, as set forth in the October 17, 2024 USPTO Non-Final Office Action.

During the telephone interview, Applicant's proposed amendments to claims 2, 3, and 16 were discussed with regard to the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejections. The Examiner indicated that the proposed amendments overcome the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejections.

In addition, during the telephone interview, rejoinder of withdrawn claims 10-15 was discussed, and the Examiner indicated that since independent claim 10 includes the structure of allowed independent claim 1, independent claim 10 would be allowed, and since dependent claims 11-15 depend from independent claim 10, such dependent claims 11-15 would also be allowed. The minor amendment to withdrawn claim 11, similar to the amendment to dependent claim 2, was also discussed.

The Examiner further indicated that once a formal response is received, he would review and consider the amended claims, and he would contact Applicant's representative by telephone should any further minor claim amendments be necessary to advance prosecution of the subject application.

As indicated above, with this Amendment and Response, claims 2, 3, 11, and 16 have been amended. Claims 10-15 were previously withdrawn. Claims 1-20 are pending. No new matter has been added with the claim amendments.

Applicant does not disclaim any subject matter by amending the claims. Applicant rescinds any implied disclaimer that may arise because of amendments to the claims. Furthermore, Applicant's arguments are not an implied waiver or disclaimer of any claimed subject matter. Applicant respectfully reserves the right to pursue these and other claims in one
or more continuing applications, including any claims that were originally filed with this application.
In the October 17, 2024 USPTO Non-Final Office Action, the Examiner rejected claims 2-3 and 16-20 under 35 U.S.C. 112(b), as being indefinite for the following reasons:

1. Claim 2 - Dependent claim 2 recites "a high-contoured composite structure", and is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) on the basis that, "[I]t is unclear what the metes and bounds of these subjective limitations are", and the definition of "high-contoured composite structures" defined in paragraph [0085] of Applicant's specification "is still unclear what would and would not read on highly contoured or a complex contour."

As indicated above, Applicant has amended dependent claim 2 to delete the term "a high- contoured composite structure". Applicant submits that this amendment to dependent claim 2 overcomes the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of dependent claim 2, and Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of dependent claim 2.

In addition, as indicated above, in the January 3, 2025 telephone interview between the Examiner and Applicant's representative, the Examiner indicated that the proposed amendment to dependent claim 2 overcomes the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).

2. Claim 3 - Dependent claim 3 recites "a high-contour kitting tray", and is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) on the basis that, "[I]t is unclear what the metes and bounds of these subjective limitations are", and the definition of "high-contoured composite structures" defined in paragraph [0085] of Applicant's specification "is still unclear what would and would not read on highly contoured or a complex contour."

As indicated above, Applicant has amended dependent claim 3 to amend "a high-contour kitting tray" to "a contoured kitting tray". Applicant submits that this amendment to dependent claim 3 overcomes the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of dependent claim 3, and Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of dependent claim 3.

In addition, as indicated above, in the January 3, 2025 telephone interview between the Examiner and Applicant's representative, the Examiner indicated that the proposed amendment to dependent claim 3 overcomes the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).

In addition, in the October 17, 2024 USPTO Non-Final Office Action, the Examiner rejected claim 3 as "grammatically awkward so as to be confusing, and it is unclear in view of Applicant's disclosure whether the kitting tray includes the straight flat kitting tray and the high contour kitting tray, or if the kitting tray comprises only one of the preceding options." The Examiner indicates in the October 17, 2024 USPTO Non-Final Office Action, that, "For purposes of examination, claim 3 will be interpreted as follows: the tray assembly comprises one of a straight flat kitting tray, a contoured kitting tray, a tooling device, or a tray mandrel."

As indicated above, Applicant has amended dependent claim 3 as follows: "The pick- and-place system of claim 1, wherein the tray assembly comprises one of, a kitting tray, including a straight flat kitting tray, and a high-contour contoured kitting tray, a tooling device, and a tray mandrel."

Applicant submits that this amendment to dependent claim 3 overcomes the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of dependent claim 3, and Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of dependent claim 3.

In addition, as indicated above, in the January 3, 2025 telephone interview between the Examiner and Applicant's representative, the Examiner indicated that the proposed amendment to dependent claim 3 overcomes the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).
3. Claims 16-20 - Independent claim 16 recites "a complex curved configuration" in

the preamble, and is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) on the basis that, "[I]t is unclear what the metes and bounds of these subjective limitations are", and the definition of "complex contours" defined in paragraph [0085] of Applicant's specification "is still unclear what would and would not read on highly contoured or a complex contour."

As indicated above, Applicant has amended independent claim 16 to amend "a complex curved configuration" to "a curved configuration". Support for this amendment is found on page 11, paragraph [0083], of Applicant's originally filed application. Applicant submits that this amendment to independent claim 16 overcomes the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of independent claim 16. In addition, since dependent claims 17-20 depend from independent claim 16, Applicant submits that such dependent claims 17-20 similarly overcome the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of dependent claims 17-20. Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. 112(b) rejection of claims 16-20.

In addition, as indicated above, in the January 3, 2025 telephone interview between the Examiner and Applicant's representative, the Examiner indicated that the proposed amendment to independent claim 16 overcomes the rejection of claims 16-20 under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).

4. Claim 11 - Withdrawn dependent claim 11 recites "a high-contoured composite structure", similar to dependent claim 2. As indicated above, and similar to the amendment to dependent claim 2, Applicant has amended withdrawn dependent claim 11 to delete the term "a high-contoured composite structure".

In the October 17, 2024 USPTO Non-Final Office Action, the Examiner indicates that claims 1 and 4-9 are allowed, and that claims 2-3 and 16-20 would be allowable if rewritten to overcome the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).

Applicant acknowledges that claims 1 and 4-9 are allowed. Applicant further submits that with this Amendment and Response, claims 2-3 and 16-20, as indicated above, have been rewritten to overcome the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).

In Applicant's October 15, 2023 Response to the September 18, 2023 Election/Restriction Requirement that issued in the subject application, Applicant elected, with traverse, Group I, claims 1-9 and 16-20, drawn to a pick-and-place system, and did not elect Group II, claims 10-15, drawn to a method for transferring and installing a contoured composite structure onto a mandrel.
Under M.P.E.P. 821.04 Rejoinder:

In order to be eligible for rejoinder, a claim to a nonelected invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim. A withdrawn claim that does not require all the limitations of an allowable claim will not be rejoined. Furthermore, where restriction was required between a product and a process of making and/or using the product, and the product invention was elected and subsequently found allowable, all claims to a nonelected process invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable claim for the claims directed to that process invention to be eligible for rejoinder. See MPEP § 821.04(b). In order to retain the right to rejoinder, applicant is advised that the claims to the nonelected invention(s) should be amended during prosecution to require the limitations of the elected
invention. Failure to do so may result in a loss of the right to rejoinder.

Applicant submits that since independent claim 1 is allowed, and independent claim 10 includes the structure of allowed independent claim 1, independent claim 10 would be allowed and eligible for rejoinder. Moreover, since dependent claims 11-15 depend from independent claim 10, such dependent claims 11-15 would also be allowed and eligible for rejoinder.

In addition, as indicated above, in the January 3, 2025 telephone interview between the Examiner and Applicant's representative, the Examiner indicated that since independent claim 10 includes the structure of allowed independent claim 1, independent claim 10 would be allowed and rejoined, and since dependent claims 11-15 depend from independent claim 10, such dependent claims 11-15 would also be allowed and rejoined.
In addition, as indicated above, withdrawn claim 11 has been amended, similar to the amendment to dependent claim 2, to delete the term "a high-contoured composite structure".

Should the Examiner have any questions or should the Examiner wish to discuss any matters in connection with this Amendment and Response, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned. It is believed that no fee is due with this response. If any fee is due for added claims or other charges, please charge to Deposit Account No. 18-1730 with reference to Docket No. 20-0450-US-NP.
